senses.sense_definition: Thick, soft, wet mud or similar heavy, viscous sediment.

examples.text: The heavy rain turned the dirt path into thick <w>sludge</w> that trapped our boots.
Workers spent the morning clearing dark <w>sludge</w> from the bottom of the pond.

senses.sense_definition: Semi-solid waste material produced during industrial or wastewater treatment processes.

examples.text: The local facility must safely dispose of toxic industrial <w>sludge</w> each month.
Sewage <w>sludge</w> is often treated and converted into fertilizer for agriculture.

senses.sense_definition: Excessive administrative friction or bureaucracy that slows down processes.

examples.text: Applicants often abandon the program due to administrative <w>sludge</w> and endless paperwork.
The new policy was designed specifically to eliminate bureaucratic <w>sludge</w> in government services.

senses.sense_definition: A subgenre of heavy metal combining elements of doom metal and hardcore punk; sludge metal.

examples.text: The band blends aggressive hardcore tempos with the heavy, slow riffs typical of <w>sludge</w>.
Fans of 1990s underground rock will immediately recognize that classic New Orleans <w>sludge</w> sound.

senses.sense_definition: A sediment of accumulated minerals deposited in a steam boiler or mechanical engine.

examples.text: Failure to change the motor oil led to a severe accumulation of engine <w>sludge</w>.
The engineer had to shut down the boiler to flush out mineral <w>sludge</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A slushy mass of small floating ice pieces forming on the surface of water.

examples.text: The ship struggled to navigate through dense sea <w>sludge</w> near the polar coast.
A layer of freezing <w>sludge</w> coated the surface of the river by morning.

senses.sense_definition: A medical mnemonic for symptoms of cholinergic crisis: salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, gastrointestinal upset, and emesis.

examples.text: Medical students learn the acronym <w>SLUDGE</w> to memorize the signs of organophosphate poisoning.
The emergency physician rapidly recognized the toxidrome using the classic <w>SLUDGE</w> mnemonic.

senses.sense_definition: To drip, ooze, or flow in a slow and sloppy manner.

examples.text: Wet mortar <w>sludged</w> down the side of the wall before the builder could wipe it away.
Cold gravy <w>sludged</w> out of the container onto the plate.

senses.sense_definition: To slump, slouch, or move in a heavy and sluggish posture.

examples.text: Exhausted from the march, the soldiers <w>sludged</w> onto their benches.
He <w>sludged</w> in the armchair after a long night at work.
